verdict.rationale: First-party docs say Claude builds a first version from a described visual, can generate a dozen directions in minutes, and supports refinement through conversation, inline comments, direct edits, and Claude-made sliders. Hands-on users corroborate this: one shipped a landing page in a few hours, another praised its quick variations, and another called the designs beautiful. Some users found output from simple prompts underwhelming or boring, which is a quality complaint rather than evidence the capability is missing. Missing for 10: consistent hands-on evidence of high output quality (mixed reports on prompt-generated results), and evidence of the final 20% of polish without manual judgment. [2026-09-30 judge-migration owner-product bias audit: quality trimmed q9 -> q7. The verdict itself is clearly supported (rich on-story first-party docs plus positive hands-on corroboration), but three cited negative hands-on reports (comm-3 'very underwhelming', comm-9 'boring' output, comm-15 unmaintainable generated code) are more than the 'exactly one minor gap' q9 requires — same bar as the claude-code natural-language-feature-implementation trim in this wave. Anthropic-affiliation governance, README §9.]
